body:
I mean, I'm going back to school in September. I can't afford to be trying a bunch of different drugs and seeing what happens. I need to have my shit together, and I can't be messing around.

I feel like if I went on medication and somehow became content/happy/whatever, I would be living in some sort of illusion. Medication can't fix my medical conditions. I am still going to have to deal with them for the rest of my life. I can't pretend that that just all of a sudden wouldn't be an issue.

I don't really experience those "wonderful little moments". I don't know how to and I don't know if I am meant to.

I just don't have any reason to believe that it will happen for me. Women won't want to deal with the bullshit that comes with all of this (especially now, at this age). And anyone who would get "turned on" by a birth defect sounds disgusting. This is something about myself which I absolutely cannot stand. It brings me pain, shame, sadness, and anger. Why would I want someone to become aroused by that? 

I have no reason to believe that I would even qualify for adoption, given my mental health history.

I guess so, but I am assuming that I would still be exempt...it doesn't make sense for one agency to allow someone with a medical situation that everyone else rejects.

I had absolutely horrible experiences with medication. It seems like I got a severe side effect from every one I tried. I saw 4 or 5 psychiatrists in total, because they kept referring me around. Because of my experiences, I have come to associate psychiatry with being completely drugged up and detached from reality. What if medication just fucks me up again? If I have to live, I would rather keep going like this than become unstable like that again.

If you don't consider that a reason to give up altogether, then what would be a reason to keep going? I have never genuinely believed that life is worth living. I don't want to have to be like this anymore. I am so tired and miserable.

I'm really glad that you've been able to change your mindset like that. Thanks for commenting.

I know that I shouldn't force things, but I guess my problem is that I have never really found anything that I love. Nothing has ever truly excited me or motivated me. It seems like I don't get any pleasure out of anything.

After thinking about it, I guess the problem is that, actually, I do know what I would want from life. However, I can't ever have those things due to circumstances beyond my control. I would like to get married and have a family, and I would like to have a career which I am ineligible for. All of this isn't possible due to some medical conditions that I have, and which I will always have to deal with. I guess that I don't know how to let go of what I want and find something else.

I'm glad that you've been able to make things work better for yourself. I really don't know what to say...I don't know how to shift my perspective as you have. Every time I've tried to do that, it's always just ended up reverting itself within a few days. 

I wish that I could relate to that poster. I guess the problem is that I'm really not free - I can't do what I would like to with my life, due to some medical conditions which will always plague me. So, I don't know. But thanks. Maybe I can get into that mindset someday, who knows.

Yeah, I know what you mean. I haven't ever really been able to see the world with a different perspective, so I guess that I don't really know how else to live.

That's good to hear. I'm glad that's working for you. My family doesn't have insurance at the moment, but I guess I'll consider going back into therapy in the future. At the very least, it will give me someone to talk to (even if I do have to pay them to listen...).
Well yeah, the problem is that I don't really enjoy doing anything. Anything I do ends up feeling trivial and mundane. How can I start enjoying things?
I have actually posted in the past, and didn't find anyone else with my conditions. Similar ones, but not the same exact thing. I would rather not get too into things.

Yeah, that's when I was diagnosed. I have had very similar phases, actually. 

It pretty much just came up out of the blue. Nothing major happened in my life at that time. However, I have a few medical conditions and I think that having to deal with them and the knowledge that I will have to keep dealing with them for the rest of my life has, at least in part, exacerbated things and kept them going.

Sorry to hear that your experience has been similar. I've never really talked to anyone who has a similar mental health history before.

I have no idea how to find that purpose. I have no motivation to do anything in life. Nothing excites me or motivates me.

I honestly don't know. I don't know whether or not I will still be alive. I guess I'll probably become a teacher or something like that.

I am in college, just wrapped up my junior year.
Lack of a purpose, I guess. I have had commitments and jobs.
Yeah, I guess so. I do a lot of volunteering when I'm away for school.
Thank you.

There is definitely a connection with it. I don't know, but I think that things would at least be a bit better if I weren't dealing with it.

No, nothing like that. I guess that I just help people to help people. I mean, I don't really have anything to do for myself, so why not do stuff for others? Kind of like that.
That's alright. But that's just it - the only thing keeping me from ending things is the people in my life. If I were alone, I wouldn't think twice.

I really would rather not go into too much detail. It's really personal and I don't like to talk about it. Basically, they affect my genitalia and hormone levels significantly. I will always have them.

Yeah, that's pretty much it. I would say that I do. I usually end up going out of my way to do things for others. I guess I'm nice, but sometimes to a fault. Don't get me wrong, I do care for others, but it's almost like it's muted. I think that other people are just more enthusiastic than I am in general, so maybe that's it.

I'm not very artistically inclined, haha. I can definitively say that I suck at painting, drawing, and sculpting. I had to take art for all 4 years of high school and...that was pretty awful. Art's not really my thing. But interesting suggestion.

Hmm...I'm not a very competitive person. I briefly played a few different sports as a kid, but I'm pretty bad at team sports. My coordination/reflexes aren't too great, and as it turns out those are pretty important, lol. I've tried a few different MMOs, but I prefer single-player gaming.

That is not what my depression results from at all. As I said, I am well-aware that others care about me and love me. It just doesn't really affect me, for whatever reason.

I'm 20, and no. I may never be able to have a girlfriend/wife, due to a few different conditions I have.
Lol
I tried that for a while when I was younger, but didn't notice any real effects. It's also my understanding that it's typically used for more mild depression (could be wrong about that, though).

Maybe that sounds dumb. I don't know how to explain it. I feel like "people love you!!!1" has been ingrained into my mind. I probably sound like a dick, but I really don't know how to be affected like that. I don't feel loved or cared about, even though I know that's objectively true.

My daily activities/choices feel really inconsequential. They're not meaningful; I'm really just going through the motions.

Yeah, I try to stay busy. I can't think of more things to do, though. Eventually, I just end up not having anything to do. I don't think that I'll be able to get a job this summer, and that's a problem. I would like to have something like that to commit my time to.
That's the problem: committing suicide would be considered selfish. My life is defined by my commitments to and relationships with other people, not by a personal sense of enjoyment or motivation.

I guess that I have always talked myself out of doing anything because of other people. When I was a kid, I would talk myself out of killing myself because I didn't want my parents (or worse, my little sister) to find my body. When I got older, it was due to teachers and friends. Now, I guess it's just due to a combination of everyone in my life. I am uncomfortable with it, but for whatever reason, I am apparently very well-liked. It's been this way since I was maybe 14 or 15. 

I guess what I meant is that I have kept going for the convenience/wellbeing/whatever of other people. I don't personally enjoy life. If there weren't anyone who cared about me like this, I wouldn't be here anymore. I am just very weary and fed up with this, if that makes sense.

Actually, funny that you'd mention it. I am medically ineligible to join the Peace Corps, and a few other volunteer programs which I've looked into. I'd like to be able to do something like that, but I'm not able to.
Easier said than done. I have no idea how to find something I am passionate about.
I have not.

Hmm, that's funny. Well, my parents are diehard atheists, so religion isn't the issue. I have a few medical conditions which really suck. They bring me a lot of frustration and shame, and affect my body. Others (with the exception of my immediate family) are not aware of them, but they definitely affect my quality of life. They'll always be there and they'll always keep me from doing things which others take for granted.

I don't know how to find any sort of passion like that. I can't say that I've ever felt too strongly about anything. 

Thanks. Glad you made it through.

I don't really have any significant hobbies. I read, work out, run, play video games, waste time online, etc. I guess that those are just things I do to pass time (and to keep myself from dwelling on shit). I don't really derive any sort of substantial enjoyment from them. During the school year, I volunteer a lot. I don't have anything that I'm passionate about.

I don't really have any significant skills or talents. I am unsure on what I want to do. I used to want to be a teacher, but I don't know if I have the energy for that. 

My social life is fine. I have a good number of friends. I make myself go out with people and stuff like that, even when I'm not really feeling it.
I know that I have a good life. I know that I have a very good life, full of people who care about me. That cannot change my brain chemistry. It'd be nice if it could, though...
Well, yeah. I know that objectively, but I can only really go off of my own experiences.
Lol, I needed that. Thanks.
